extracted.intended_audience: healthcare communications professionals, PR teams, healthcare organizations and marketers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and executing public relations in the healthcare sector, including proactive storytelling, crisis comms, regulatory compliance, media relations, and measurement. Focused on healthcare organizations, agencies, and in-house PR teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Focuses on building a positive reputation through education, awareness campaigns, and thought leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use blogs, podcasts, videos, infographics, patient success stories and expert Q&As to educate audiences and humanize the brand. Tie content across platforms so information is easy to find and understand (example: Mayo Clinic's integrated social approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reactive PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding to crises, addressing misinformation, and managing public concerns in real-time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have pre-established protocols and tools to respond quickly; monitor misinformation and correct it to prevent harm to public health. Speed and accuracy are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building trust and credibility (transparency and ethical messaging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honest, patient-centered communication that avoids sensationalism and ensures claims are backed by reputable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly disclose potential risks or limitations of treatments/services. Prioritize transparency in messaging and regular updates on medical advancements, policy changes, and guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing public perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight medical advancements, patient success stories, and organizational mission to shape public perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use storytelling and factual reporting to reinforce reputation; ensure portrayal is accurate and supported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication and reputation management
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide immediate, transparent, fact-based responses during crises (e.g., recalls, data breaches, public health emergencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a structured response plan with pre-established protocols for different crisis types, designated spokespeople, clear channels for public/media communication, active monitoring of media coverage and sentiment, and coordination with government agencies when appropriate. Act fast and decisively; prioritize safety and transparency (Tylenol case example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient and stakeholder communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure patients, healthcare providers, investors, and regulators receive clear, accurate, and timely updates on treatments, policies, and care improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor messaging to the audience's needs; maintain timeliness and accuracy; work closely with internal stakeholders to align communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting research and education
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate complex medical research into accessible information for the public and promote disease prevention and new treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote research findings in plain language, contextualize results, and work with researchers to ensure accuracy. Use campaigns and educational content to increase public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media training for spokespeople
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare medical professionals to deliver clear, accurate, and empathetic communication during interviews and public appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train on message discipline, empathy, avoiding jargon, and handling difficult or sensitive questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent and transparent messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular openness about treatments, risks, and innovations to establish credibility and reinforce public confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide routine updates and ensure internal alignment so external messages remain consistent across channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert-backed information
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborate with medical professionals to validate claims and provide science-based content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work closely with doctors, researchers, and regulatory bodies to ensure communications are scientifically accurate and ethically sound; cite reputable sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Host public forums, patient testimonials, and health education campaigns to foster direct engagement and address community concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage dialogue, solicit feedback, and use community inputs to inform messaging and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation management (proactive misinformation addressing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactively address misinformation, clarify misunderstandings, and maintain a responsible online presence to protect long-term trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively monitor public sentiment, perform proactive media outreach, and correct false narratives quickly and transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to laws and regulations such as HIPAA (US) and GDPR (Europe) to protect patient privacy and avoid severe legal consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with legal and compliance teams when crafting messages; ensure no patient-identifiable information is shared without explicit consent; maintain records and processes that demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and accurate communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Healthcare messaging must be science-backed and free from misleading claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensationalism and promotional claims unsupported by evidence; disclose limitations and potential risks; ensure alignment with ethical standards in healthcare communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration with medical professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: PR teams must work closely with doctors, researchers, and subject-matter experts to ensure clarity and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage experts early for message development, review scientific claims, and involve them in media interactions and thought leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital PR and social media best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use digital platforms (blogs, podcasts, videos, infographics, social posts) to inform and engage while complying with data protection and ethical rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate content across platforms, answer questions, run interactive campaigns, avoid sharing patient-identifiable data without consent, continuously monitor and correct misinformation, and align messaging with legal/privacy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations and thought leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Position healthcare professionals as industry experts through press releases, expert interviews, op-eds, speaking engagements, and relationships with journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide journalists with reliable, science-backed information; build long-term media relationships; use thought leadership to enhance credibility and awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the right media channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose channels that best reach and influence target audiences—traditional media for credibility and digital platforms for real-time engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a multi-channel approach combining press releases, journals, TV, social media, blogs, webinars, and events to maximize reach and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify key messages and target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the core message you want to convey and tailor it to specific audiences (patients, healthcare professionals, government agencies, investors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment audiences and adapt tone, detail level, and channel choice to match their concerns and information needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and measure impact (KPIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use analytics tools to track audience engagement, media coverage, and public sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track KPIs such as press mentions, social media engagement, website traffic, and audience feedback; regularly analyze metrics to adjust messaging and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage PR platforms and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PR software (example: Prezly) to streamline press release distribution, media tracking, stakeholder engagement, and crisis readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain centralized media contact databases, create crisis newsrooms and emergency lists in advance, use built-in analytics for measurement, and collaborate within the team for timely responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to hire a healthcare PR agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider external agencies for specialized support with media outreach, crisis management, and regulatory navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess agency fit based on industry expertise, regulatory knowledge, media connections, proven results (case studies/testimonials), and their ability to provide a tailored strategic approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for choosing a healthcare PR agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Key factors include industry expertise, regulatory knowledge, media connections, proven results, and strategic approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look beyond client lists—seek demonstrated experience in your specific healthcare area and evidence of measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keeping control of PR strategy when working with agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Even with an agency, the organization should stay involved in PR efforts and message decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tools to maintain oversight, participate in strategy development, and ensure alignment with internal goals and compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act fast and decisively in crises
rubrics_metrics.description: Delays worsen crises; speed in decisions and communication is critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have processes and tools ready to launch crisis communications in seconds/hours (e.g., emergency contact lists, pre-approved messaging templates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety-first principle in crisis response
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize public safety over profits or defensive positioning during health crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take actions (recalls, warnings, halting production) when necessary and communicate those actions openly; use safety-focused measures to rebuild trust (Tylenol example: tamper-proof packaging, open CEO communications).
